reason: The ACP file-write gate and the compaction-event handling are two halves of one client: what the dispatch runner must gate and what it must advertise and receive from each agent adapter. A maintainer would write one ACP client skill with labeled sections. The per-adapter write-path table moves to references/.

The person told the agent not to lock files until rules and prompts exist, or to disable the code. The lock, its prompt line and its ask rule were coupled to no single switch, so turning it off left agents with a stale sandbox warning.

Rich's 2026-10-15 instruction: no file lock until its rules and prompts exist. The lock switch was off, yet the held settings still sent the Claude ask rules, so every edit was still gated. The ask rule must read the same switch as the refusal.

The switch covered the refusal, rule line, Codex read-only and terminal, but one settings site (the Claude ask rule) was missed on the first pass and found only when Rich asked again. A per-site audit prevents a second miss.

Repair for my previous intent: its new_string was a bare placeholder "x" that would have erased the Claude ask-rule sentence. This intent lands after it (in order) and restores the sentence with the switch condition added.
Sandbox behaviour and Codex approval shapes were measured this episode and decide how the write gate classifies requests; the skill had the gate rules but not these measured facts.
